acceptance_criteria: [AC-3, R1] lib/readiness_contract.py (sha256 30cfb9bf7436ff1f6b14c0b16542a62a6893321f5eface820c827ae4ec600166), lib/verification.py (572819a9c8a1039173c5483d0f7f9a33362588d197e27731bb97b5dd78d33524), schemas/readiness-contract.json (f05119f6d00d2d2cf58270c81073e70016d2644042e3f8185ac0371ef88aa384) and both readiness-dependency.json files are byte-identical to the base commit; tests/readiness_v1_freeze_test.sh pins these digests and replays a golden corpus of v1 admit/publish/migrate JSON outputs captured at the base commit (skills fixtures plus a copy of the registered xskp-p5 generation), asserting byte-identical output; red before the corpus exists, green after.

[AC-3] The existing v1 suites (readiness_contract, readiness_scoped, readiness_mapped, readiness_worktree, readiness_merge_driver, autobahn_run_gates, autobahn_worktree_run_gates, northstar_handoff) pass unmodified. The single exception is tests/autobahn_merge_authority_test.sh: only its working directory changes, from cd "$REPO_ROOT" to a temporary git repository with no v2 artifacts (with SCRIPT and the committed verdict fixture resolved against REPO_ROOT), every existing assertion stays byte-identical, and one appended case asserts that a verdict-only call is refused once that temporary repository's origin/main carries a v2 registry. Without this, P-S2's v2 registry on skills origin/main would refuse every verdict-only case and bash tests/run-tests.sh would fail in every skills goal. contract-run.sh's route prelude dispatches only v2 operation names to contract-run-v2.sh.

[G2, P1] lib/readiness_contract_v2.py validates readiness-policy/2 at the fixed path: repository{id}, identity_model (multi|single), sources[] (paths; digests observed), required_checks[], skippable_checks[], branch_pattern, target, tools[], reviewer_requirements{independent_lane:true}, approval{anchor_sha256,max_age_days:14,accept}, gates[]; only the 10 fixed gate kinds; repository-scoped gates only; not_applicable only for fixture and harness_trust with reason no-fixture-dependency or no-pinned-harness. A goal-scoped gate, unknown kind or field, extensions.active_plan, or any bundle-supplied gate is refused with a named code.

[O1, P2, R2b] goal_revision_v2 hashes only id, scope, acceptance_criteria, dependencies (by id), verification and repository.id; goals.json is content-only and bundle_sha256 is its content hash; the approval binds generation_v2 (content, spec, policy, anchor) and the sidecar_v0 digest; the sidecar holds only readiness holds, coverage, legacy_safe_tdd and legacy_risk_reason (owner lives in the approval), ordered per field (readiness unknown < blocked; legacy_safe_tdd false < true; legacy_risk_reason by prefix extension; coverage unknown < measured with a final percent) and as their product; admission refuses a sidecar that is not >= sidecar_v0.

[AC-4, O1] tests/readiness_v2_core_test.py proves both directions: (a) tightening sidecar edits (hold added, coverage measured, legacy_risk_reason extended) leave generation_v2 and the approval valid; (b) scope or acceptance_criteria edits change generation_v2 and invalidate the approval; (c) loosening edits (hold removed, legacy_safe_tdd true to false) are refused until a new approval binds a new sidecar_v0.

[U1, R2, K1, O4] plan-approval/1 is canonical JSON with plan_id, generation, bundle_sha256, spec_sha256, policy_sha256, sidecar_sha256, goals[], stages [implementation, merge], owner, reviewer_lane, issued_at, expires_at, anchor_sha256 and assurance; it is carried by exactly one unsigned annotated tag approval/<plan_id>/<generation[0:12]> (with the detached ai-catapult-plan-approval signature for ssh-tag, or the digest-echo record for in-session), which is authoritative. The observer locates the anchor via the passwd home directory (a test-only in-process locator hook exists; no env var or flag) and runs ssh-keygen -Y verify; roles come from the allowed_signers namespaces= option (approver: ai-catapult-plan-approval; agent: ai-catapult-review,ai-catapult-certificate).

[AC-2, U1, R2, R2b, K1] tests/readiness_v2_approval_test.py uses ephemeral keys and a temporary anchor and refuses: a forged signature, an agent-namespace principal, an approval older than 14 days or past expires_at, a changed generation/spec/policy/sidecar digest, a missing anchor, an anchor inside any git worktree, and an anchor whose sha256 differs from policy.approval.anchor_sha256. ssh-tag assurance is user-presence only for an sk- key whose anchor line lacks no-touch-required; an sk- key with no-touch-required and any non-sk key report key-held.

[O2, K2] With accept ["ssh-tag", "in-session"] an in-session digest-echo record is accepted, including for policy bootstrap and U3 admin merges, and is always reported as assurance in-session; with accept narrowed to ["ssh-tag"] the same record is refused. Every approval, admission report, certificate, merge-authority decision and audit entry carries assurance, in-session is printed prominently, and a test asserts no code path renders in-session or key-held as user-presence.

[O9, O3, P1] Policy bootstrap: only when origin/<target> has no live readiness-policy/2, a generation may carry an immutable policy-candidate.json bound by the approval's policy_sha256; exactly one policy goal may scope the fixed path and every sibling must depend on it; the policy goal is admitted against the full candidate, which stays inert until the approval verifies; its certificate requires the head file to equal policy_sha256. Negative tests refuse a candidate while policy/2 is live, two policy-scoped goals, a non-dependent sibling, and a differing head policy.

[G3, P3, P4, P6] lib/observer.py emits observation/1 facts with source, observed_at and commit: tool presence, file digests, B5 git_ancestor of planning inputs on origin/<target>, transitive dependency completion as git_ancestor of each ancestor goal's PR merge commit (squash merges included), repository identity as repository.id plus observed git common-dir, PR head and base, required checks (deduplicated by name across push and pull_request runs; every run at head must conclude SUCCESS, SKIPPED only for skippable_checks), unresolved threads, branch-protection required checks (unavailable on 403/404, never counted as satisfied), and the agent-signed review lane record.

[G3, AC-2] The validator is pure (tests patch subprocess and file writes to raise and it still decides). admit-v2 rebuilds the readiness context itself from fresh observation plus the verified approval; a supplied readiness-context/2, observation/1 or verdict that differs from the rebuilt one is refused, and an agent-written one is never used as input.

[Structural] Every v2 entry point exits 2 on an unknown argument and builds its environment from an allowlist: it passes through only PATH, LANG, LC_ALL, TMPDIR, SSH_AUTH_SOCK and GH_TOKEN (if present), and sets HOME and GH_CONFIG_DIR from the passwd home directory (never inherited) so keyring-authenticated gh works; a test proves everything else is dropped (GH_HOST, GH_REPO, GH_ENTERPRISE_*, GIT_DIR and other GIT_*, an inherited HOME, AI_FACTORY_ALLOW_UNREACHABLE_UMBRELLA, SKIP_*) and that the production hosted adapter still runs gh under it; the adapter is injected in-process only for tests and recorded in every observation and certificate.

[U2, U3, O4, O7, P7] run-gates.sh --phase pre-merge on a v2 bundle issues merge-certificate/1 only when, at one exact head with a clean tree, it binds the approval digest and assurance, PR number, head and base SHAs, merge-stage admission digest, local gate results, every required check SUCCESS completed before issue, zero unresolved threads, a review lane record signed by an agent principal distinct from the implementing lane (lane_independence: declared), and an admin flag only under identity_model single. The certificate is agent-signed, stored in observer state, and every driver exit code is appended to the observer-state driver log.

[U2, U3, AC-2, K2] merge-authority.sh makes --pr mandatory on every call, --verdict included, whenever origin/<target> of the repository it runs in has a v2 registry (.ai/workflows/northstar-readiness-v2.json) or a live readiness-policy/2; with --pr it selects v1 or v2 by observing the PR's head branch against that v2 registry, so a verdict-only call can never take the v1 path for a v2 PR. For v2 it refuses --verdict, re-runs the local gates and re-observes every hosted fact rather than trusting certificate claims, and refuses on any difference, a moved head, an expired approval, a missing certificate, a non-production adapter, or a self-review-only admin merge. Merges use gh pr merge --match-head-commit, and every decision records assurance. tests/autobahn_merge_authority_test.sh keeps exercising the v1 path by running in a temporary git repository with neither a v2 registry nor policy/2 (its only change, see AC-3), so its assertions stay byte-identical after skills origin/main gains a v2 registry; a merge-authority call made outside the target repository takes the v1 path, and audit-merges still flags any v2 PR merged without a certificate. tests/readiness_v2_certificate_test.py covers: moved head (including between observation and merge), pending check, unlisted SKIPPED, unresolved thread, missing lane, self-review-only admin, a v2 PR given --verdict, a verdict-only call without --pr in a repository whose origin/<target> has a v2 registry or policy/2 (refused, never exit 0), and a forged certificate signed by a valid agent key whose claims are false.

[Proceed semantics, AC-2] The certificate test feeds 'proceed', 'override', '--admin if necessary', --force and SKIP_*-style variables to every v2 entry point and asserts every gate is still evaluated and refusals stand.

[P8] readiness-dependency-v2.json (identical in autobahn and northstar) pins lib/readiness_contract_v2.py, lib/observer.py, lib/readiness_contract.py, lib/verification.py, schemas/readiness-contract-v2.json, contract-run.sh, contract-run-v2.sh, run-gates.sh, merge-authority.sh, prereq-check.sh, migrate-handoff.sh and northstar's handoff-write.sh; the v2 driver and observer run from the target-branch base commit's copy verified against it, and a test proves a PR editing these files is admitted by the base copy, never its own head.
